title: Chesapeake seafood seasoning
desc: A homemade Old Bay-style blend: celery seed and bay leaf ground fresh, sweet paprika, black pepper, dry mustard, cayenne, and a small amount of warm spice (allspice, clove, mace, ginger, cardamom, cinnamon), cut with fine sea salt. The celery seed and bay carry it; the warm spices sit underneath.

title: Maryland crab cakes
desc: Jumbo lump blue crab held together by the minimum binder that will hold it: one egg, a spoon of mayonnaise, dijon, Worcestershire, Chesapeake seasoning, and a handful of crushed saltines. Chilled to set, then seared hard in butter and oil so the outside goes deep golden while the inside stays loose, sweet, and almost all crab.

ingredients.item: jumbo lump blue crab meat, refrigerated (not shelf-stable)

title: Tartar sauce
desc: Mayonnaise sharpened with minced cornichons, capers, shallot, lemon zest and juice, dill, and a little of the pickle brine. A cold, briny, high-acid sauce built to cut fried and seared seafood.

title: Vinegar coleslaw
desc: Finely shredded green cabbage and carrot, salted briefly to pull out surface water, then dressed with cider vinegar, a little sugar, oil, dijon, and celery seed. Crunchy, sharp, and mayonnaise-free, so it cuts rich seafood and fried food instead of adding to it.

ingredients.item: green cabbage, cored and finely shredded

title: Blue crab
desc: Atlantic swimming crab, Callinectes sapidus, from the Chesapeake Bay to the Gulf of Mexico. Sweet, briny, finely flaked white meat sold live, steamed whole, or picked and graded by the part of the body it comes from.

title: Roasted butternut squash salad with radicchio, pecans, and balsamic
desc: Hard-roasted butternut cubes, dressed hot so they drink the vinaigrette, laid over radicchio and arugula with salted toasted pecans, crisped sage, and shaved parmigiano. Sweetness comes only from the caramelized squash and the balsamic; bitter leaves, a red wine vinegar spine, and a salty umami finish keep it a savory side rather than a dessert on a plate.

title: Nuoc cham bun cha (Hanoi-style warm dipping broth)
desc: The Hanoi version of nuoc cham, served warm in a deep bowl as a thin, light broth rather than a dip. Fish sauce, rice vinegar, and sugar are dissolved in a generous volume of hot water, then loaded with quick-pickled green papaya and carrot, raw garlic, and chili. Grilled pork and patties go straight into the bowl, and diners dip rice vermicelli and herbs through it.

title: Nuoc cham chay (vegan dipping sauce)
desc: The Buddhist temple-kitchen nuoc cham, built without fish. Light soy sauce and a strong dried-shiitake soaking liquid stand in for the fish sauce, fresh coconut water gives the gentle sweetness and body southern cooks use in place of plain water, and lime, garlic, and chili finish it exactly like the original.

title: Nuoc mam gung (ginger fish sauce)
desc: The ginger-heavy nuoc cham served with poached chicken, boiled duck, and steamed fish. Fresh ginger is pounded with sugar in a mortar until it weeps juice, then loosened with fish sauce, lime, and a little water. Thicker, hotter on the palate, and less diluted than everyday nuoc cham, so it clings to plain poached meat that has no seasoning of its own.

title: Nuoc mam me (tamarind fish sauce)
desc: The southern Vietnamese sweet-sour dip for crab, snails, grilled shrimp, and fried fish. Tamarind pulp is dissolved and strained, then reduced with palm sugar into a glossy brown syrup and finished off heat with fish sauce, fried garlic, and chili. Thicker and deeper than lime-based nuoc cham, with a fruity, rounded sourness that clings to shellfish.

title: Tuong ot (Vietnamese chili-garlic sauce, Chin-su style)
desc: The smooth, glossy, sweet-hot chili-garlic sauce that sits in a squeeze bottle on every pho and banh mi counter in Vietnam, best known by the Chin-su brand. Fresh red chilies and a heavy garlic load are simmered in a light sugar-vinegar brine, blended, sieved, and set with a small tapioca slurry into a pourable, cling-to-the-spoon sauce. Sweeter, brighter, and more garlic-forward than Thai-style sriracha, with no fermentation and no tomato.

ingredients.item: fresh red Fresno or long red chilies

title: Cod and crisp potatoes in rosemary-anchovy cream
desc: A one-skillet cod and potato bake. The cream sauce is built on dissolved anchovy and a white wine reduction, so it carries glutamate and acid before any cream goes in. The potatoes are parboiled in alkaline water and roasted hard so their crust sits above the sauce line, and fried capers with toasted panko replace the soft garnish of the original.

title: Black bean and sweet potato chili
desc: Black beans simmered in a purée of toasted ancho and chipotle, built on cremini mushrooms cooked until they brown and stick, which gives the pot the savory depth that meat would. Sweet potato is roasted separately so it caramelizes and keeps its shape instead of dissolving.

ingredients.item: kosher salt, for the sweet potato
chipotle chiles in adobo, with sauce

title: Carne adovada
desc: Pork shoulder marinated overnight in a sauce made from one chile, the dried New Mexico red pod, then baked covered for 3 hours until it falls apart in a thick, brick-red sauce. Earthy and clean rather than smoky or heavily spiced: almost no cumin, no tomato, and a little vinegar and honey to balance the chile.

title: Chile verde con puerco
desc: Pork shoulder seared in lard and braised in a salsa of broiled tomatillos, poblano, Anaheim, and jalapeño chiles. The tomatillos supply both the acid and the body; charring them first trades their raw sourness for a sweeter, smoky depth.

title: Chunky beef and bean chili
desc: Store-bought chili-cut beef, salted ahead and browned in bacon fat, braised with a purée of toasted ancho, guajillo, and chipotle in adobo, then finished with kidney beans and a masa-thickened gravy. A shorter braise than a whole-chuck chili because the pieces are small, and a lid on the pot because chili-cut packs often include leaner round.

ingredients.item: chipotle chiles in adobo, with sauce
cooked dark red kidney beans, drained

title: Cincinnati chili
desc: Ground beef broken into cold water rather than browned, so it cooks into a fine, saucy texture, then simmered for hours with ancho, cinnamon, allspice, cloves, cumin, and cocoa. Served over spaghetti under a heap of finely shredded cheddar, in the Greek-Macedonian tradition of Cincinnati chili parlors.

ingredients.item: kosher salt, for the pasta water

title: Kidney beans from dried
desc: Dark red kidney beans brine-soaked overnight, boiled hard for 10 minutes to destroy their natural toxin, then held at a bare simmer with onion, garlic, bay, and kombu until creamy inside with intact skins. The same method works for pinto beans.

title: White chicken chili
desc: Browned chicken thighs simmered in stock with broiled poblano, Anaheim, and jalapeño chiles and creamy white beans, then shredded. Mashed beans and a spoonful of crema give the broth body without flour, and lime keeps it bright. Turkey works the same way.

title: Braising
desc: Cook collagen-rich meat or dense vegetables partly submerged in liquid, covered, below a boil for hours, until connective tissue converts to gelatin and the liquid becomes the sauce.

title: Mexican crema
desc: Heavy cream cultured with a spoonful of buttermilk at room temperature until it thickens to a pourable, lightly sour cream, then finished with salt and lime. Higher in fat than sour cream, so it does not curdle on hot stews or salsa.

title: Basque burnt cheesecake
desc: The La Viña tarta de queso from San Sebastián: cream cheese, sugar, eggs, heavy cream and a spoonful of flour, baked crustless in a parchment-lined springform at high heat until the top scorches nearly black and the center stays a loose, creamy custard. Five ingredients, one bowl, and the oven does the work.

ingredients.item: full-fat cream cheese (block, not tub), room temperature

equipment: stand mixer with paddle (or a large bowl and wooden spoon)

title: Zhajiangmian (Beijing fried-sauce noodles)
desc: Diced pork belly rendered in a wok, then fried slowly in a 2:1 blend of yellow soybean paste and sweet bean sauce until the paste darkens and the oil separates out around it. The salty, glossy sauce goes over hot fresh wheat noodles with piles of raw cucumber and radish, blanched sprouts and edamame, and raw garlic and black vinegar at the table.

title: Birria de res with consomé
desc: Beef chuck and oxtail marinated overnight in a guajillo, ancho, and chile de árbol adobo with vinegar, toasted spices, and charred tomato, then braised for four hours until the meat falls apart and the bones have turned the liquid into a glossy, gelatin-rich consomé. Served as tacos on fat-dipped, griddled corn tortillas with a cup of consomé for dipping.

ingredients.item: corn tortillas, 12 to 15 cm / 5 to 6 inch
